title: Regional priority-constrained routing and eviction playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Design and implement a deterministic routing policy that balances latency SLOs, regional capacity, and customer affinity. Introduce a capacity-aware eviction and circuit-breaker layer to prevent cascading failures during regional overloads while preserving high-priority traffic and graceful degradation paths.
acceptance_criteria: Routing decision includes latency estimate and remaining regional capacity score for each candidate region
Requests tagged with customer affinity are respected for >= 95% of cases when regional capacity >= soft_threshold
Circuit breaker trips prevent >90% of overload-induced tail latency spikes in downstream GPUs during synthetic surge tests
Eviction policy reduces dropped high-priority requests to <1% during 2x traffic bursts while shedding low-priority requests first
End-to-end telemetry surfaces per-region p50/p95/p99 latency, per-region token budget consumption, and cache-hit-adjusted cost estimates
implementation_notes: Introduce a RegionScore computed as weighted(sum(normalized_latency_headroom, normalized_capacity_headroom, affinity_bonus))
Latency estimates derived from windowed p50/p95 for model+route pair plus network RTT estimate; default weight favors p95 during peak hours
Capacity headroom uses token-budget model: allocated_tokens - recent_5m_consumption; normalize by configured_capacity_per_region
Affinity is treated as a soft-bonus (not hard pin) with configurable hysteresis; if affinity_bonus pushes RegionScore over primary_threshold, prefer same-region routing

When RegionScore < eviction_threshold, route to fallback: either (1) quantized-model variant in same region, (2) different region with RegionScore > primary_threshold, or (3) return graceful-perf-degradation response depending on customer policy
Circuit breaker implemented as a two-tier controller: local node-level fast CB (short window) + global region-level CB (longer window) with token-bucket throttling to admission controller
Integrate with autoscaler signals: when region-level CB is active > 30s, emit scale_up_hint to autoscaler topic and raise alert
Fallback policy supports per-customer preferences: quality-first, cost-first, or latency-first (defaults to latency-first for enterprise customers)
Expose configuration via console: soft_thresholds, hard_thresholds, affinity_hysteresis_seconds, cb_window_ms, and token_bucket_rates
decisions: Use weighted RegionScore rather than strict geo-pinning to preserve availability under capacity pressure
Prefer p95-based latency estimates for steering decisions because p50 can mask tail behavior during partial failures
Evict by request-priority buckets (enterprise > standard > best-effort) rather than by random sampling
Circuit breaker thresholds based on token consumption and GPU queue length instead of only error rate
Implement graceful degradation via model variant fallback (quantized or smaller model) before outright dropping requests
Do not perform cross-tenant preemption in Dedicated pools; preemption allowed only within tenant token buckets
risks: Affinity as a soft-bonus may increase cross-region traffic and egress cost under heavy load
Incorrect normalization of capacity can oscillate routing decisions leading to flapping; requires hysteresis and damping
Model-switch fallbacks may introduce subtle output regressions; require per-tenant eval thresholds to avoid user-visible regressions
Circuit-breaker misconfiguration could either allow overload to cascade or be too aggressive and hurt availability
Autoscaler and CB race conditions: rapid CB flips could cause spiky scale events if not smoothed
testing_plan: Unit tests for RegionScore math and normalization with deterministic seeds
Integration tests with local steerbox simulator: run synthetic mixes (steady, bursty, affinity-heavy) and validate routing ratios
Chaos test: kill regional GPUs and verify failover sequence (local quantized fallback -> cross-region -> degraded-response) keeps SLO violation window < 30s
Load test: 2x sustained QPS for 10 minutes with mixed priorities to validate eviction ordering and CB behavior
Canary rollout to 10% of traffic in eu-west-1 for 48h with automated rollback on p99 latency > baseline + 35% or error rate > 0.5%
Regression evals: run representative prompt suite for any model-variant fallback to ensure quality delta within configured threshold
observability: New Grafana dashboard: routing/region_score_over_time (p50/p95/p99 per region, capacity_headroom, affinity_hit_rate)
Dashboards: per-customer routing breakdown, model-fallback-rate, per-region_token_consumption
Tracing: attach routing decision context (RegionScore components, chosen_region, fallback_reason) to request traces
SLO burn rate tracking: derive per-region burn rates and surface in console with suggested mitigation actions
dependencies_list: infra: messaging topic 'autoscaler-hints' must be provisioned
